messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: GPU instability spike detected in region fleet-east-3. Multiple driver resets (Xid 13/31) and ECC correctable errors; a subset of inference pods spilling OOMs and container exits. Alerting: high 5xx rate on text-gen-prod, KV cache thrashing observed. Auto-evac policy triggered for 4 nodes.

jordan (oncall): I'm on it. first triage: are we seeing a single node pattern or broad across the cluster?

maria (mlinfra): seeing Xid 13 + nv-host-reset entries in node-exporter logs across 6 hosts in east-3. TTL of resets ~30s, then back to normal for a bit. KV cache sizes spike right before crashes.

nate (eng-runtime): linking the driver logs from node-17: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0x4c) 13, PID=4123, GPU=0, Channel 00000001
[ 12345.679002] NVRM: GPU at 0000:af:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12346.001234] containerd: killing process 4123 (python) OOMKilled
```
This looks like a kernel/driver-level fault propagating to the container.

sylvia (sre): customer impact: 7% increase 5xx for text-gen-prod since 14:02 UTC, p99 latency up 2.3x due to retries. Notified alerting channel and opened bridge.

jordan (oncall): immediate mitigation steps I propose: 1) cordon + drain the 4 nodes exhibiting repeated Xid; 2) fallback route for traffic to dedicated fallback region (east-1) and cheaper model variant; 3) suspend auto-scaling to avoid noisy spin-up. Comments?

maria (mlinfra): agree. Add runbook snippet: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-resets — follow section "evacuation + kvcache". I'll take node cordon/drain.

nate (eng-runtime): before full drain, try disabling KV cache on the affected hosts to confirm correlation: set env var on runtime service: `KV_CACHE_DISABLED=true` and restart the runtime process on the node. If that stops the Xid recurrence, we have KV cache interplay. Quick command I ran on node-17: 
```bash
sudo systemctl stop redwood-runtime
export KV_CACHE_DISABLED=true
sudo systemctl start redwood-runtime
```
After that, node-17 had no resets for ~8m, then it came back with another Xid.

sylvia (sre): that implies partial mitigation only. Proceed with drain so we stop customer impact. I'll update SLO dashboard and post initial customer note draft.

jordan (oncall): @deploy-bot, initiate traffic re-route to east-1 fallback pool now. Marking the 4 nodes for graceful eviction.

deploy-bot: routing policy updated: redirect 22% of gen-text-prod traffic to east-1 fallback; draining nodes: node-17, node-22, node-23, node-29. ETA ~3m for session drain. :white_check_mark:

customer-bridge-bot: Created customer bridge and posted initial note to affected customer list. Suggested message: "We're investigating GPU driver resets causing intermittent errors; applying failover. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA."

maria (mlinfra): draining logs captured a pattern: large KV cache append cycles (~1.2GB bump) ~20s before driver reset. Dumped a snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T14:01:12Z kvcache: append 1.2GiB for convo 0x9a3
2026-03-15T14:01:33Z NVRM: Xid (0x4c) 13, PID=5121
```
Maybe cache compaction is provoking GPU memory pressure + driver instability on these cards.

nate (eng-runtime): plan: 1) pin runtime to conservative kernel-kmod on these nodes (revert any experimental kernel/driver flags), 2) temporarily throttle KV writes at runtime layer (quick patch applied to edge router), 3) kick off driver re-provision on drained hosts (reinstall NVIDIA driver + reboot) if further resets occur.

jordan (oncall): I'm executing the throttle now. Patching edge router config: `max_kv_write_bytes=256MB/s` then restarting rollout for router service across east-3 (canary to one node first):
```bash
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/edge-router MAX_KV_WRITE_BYTES=268435456
kubectl rollout restart deploy/edge-router -n infra --selector=zone=east-3
```
Canary looks good on node-11. Applying to rest.

sylvia (sre): customer impact update: errors dropped to 2.1% above baseline after routing + throttling. Continued monitoring.

maria (mlinfra): drained nodes show repeated ECC correctable error counters climbing just before Xid. Might be GPU hardware aging issue on that rack. 

nate (eng-runtime): I'll open a hardware ticket for nodes 17/22/23/29 with infra and request RMA eligibility. Meanwhile, I recommend we keep them cordoned and reimage one at a time after driver reflash.

jordan (oncall): Agreed. Putting an operational note for next oncall. @sylvia please prepare the post-incident customer update with timeline.

sylvia (sre): drafting now. Key points: what happened, immediate mitigations (drain + fallback + throttle), customer impact (5xx spike brief, reduced after failover), next steps (hardware RMA, driver reprovision, runbook follow-up). Will ping for review in 10m.

maria (mlinfra): small but important detail: we found one pod core dump with backtrace that references `nvme` + `nvidia_uvm`. Uploading to artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/bug/4951236789/1

nate (eng-runtime): capturing escalation notes for eng-runtime: suspected sequence = KV write spike -> UVM page fault -> driver hangs (Xid) -> kernel resets -> container OOM. We'll instrument more UVM metrics and add a guard in runtime to avoid large contiguous GPU allocations during high kvcache churn.

jordan (oncall): oncall handoff note: I'm handing off to @nate for follow-ups in the 18:00 shift. Leaving cordon/drain state and routing changes in place. If resets reappear on other racks, escalate to infra-hardware.

nate (eng-runtime): taking over. I'll coordinate driver reprovision tomorrow morning, start RMAs, and add temporary runtime guard. Will post a summary with play-by-play and root-cause hypothesis.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=SEV2 -> action=partial-failover-applied -> owner=nate (eng-runtime) -> incident_id=INC-20260315-4951236789

sylvia (sre): handoff acked. Closing live bridge, leaving the customer bridge open for updated message. Next steps logged in incident tracker. :white_check_mark:

customer-bridge-bot: Posted updated customer message: "Failover applied, majority of traffic routed to fallback region. Next update within 4 hours or when we have root-cause."

jordan (oncall): final note before handoff: keep an eye on `gpu.uvo.pagefaults` and `kvcache.append_bytes` dashboards; if either trends up, trigger full evacuation for east-3.

nate (eng-runtime): got it. I'll run the diagnostic on the remaining rack tonight and follow up in the incident tracker with a full timeline and remediation actions.

incident-bot: Bridge closed. Incident state -> monitoring.
